title: Risk rating methodology
description: The organisation has a documented method for rating risk, with defined impact and likelihood scales, so that risks are scored the same way across every department.
effectiveness_notes: This is a major benefit of running the CIRKS system

title: Risk management process
description: A documented process sets out how risks are identified, assessed, treated, accepted and reviewed, and who is involved at each stage.

title: Formalised responsibilities
description: Responsibilities for information risk are formally assigned, including a senior risk owner, information asset owners (IAOs) and risk owners, and the people named have accepted them.

title: Risk register
description: All identified risks are recorded in a central risk register, each with an owner, a rating, a treatment decision and a review date.

title: Security action plan
description: Agreed risk treatments are tracked in a security action plan with an owner, target date and progress for each action, and progress is reported to the risk owner.

title: Threats are identified
description: Threats relevant to the organisation are identified and kept up to date, using threat intelligence and contact with security groups and peers, and are used to inform risk assessments.
effectiveness_notes: We have feeds and we occasionally review these to determine if we need to improv them. But we lack resources to use the more expensive and time consuming feeds.; Mostly based on detected threats with almost no advanced analysis

title: Security control objectives
description: The organisation maintains a set of security control objectives against which controls are selected, implemented and assessed.

title: Risk acceptance
description: Risks above the organisation's risk appetite are accepted only by someone with the authority to do so, and each acceptance is recorded with its reason and an expiry date.

title: Risk reporting
description: Senior leadership receives regular reports on the organisation's risk position, including supplier risks, through clear lines of communication, so that it can make informed decisions about priorities and resources.
effectiveness_notes: This is well established as part of the SWG and ISMS processes

title: Document management lifecycle
description: Security policies, standards and procedures each have an owner, are approved, version-controlled, available to those who need them and reviewed on a set cycle.
effectiveness_notes: All in place but we have to wait for the completion of the first full cycle.

title: Scope and context
description: The organisation has defined its mission, the scope of its information risk management, the internal and external issues that affect it, the critical services others depend on and those it depends on, and what interested parties such as regulators and customers require of it.
effectiveness_notes: CIRKS provide the measurement of impact. individual RTOs and RPOs are then handled  by the Backup and Resilience policy; Mostly covered by CIRKS and the ISMS processes; This is a core analysis capability of CIRKS

title: Leadership commitment
description: Senior leadership approves the information security policy, provides the people and budget needed, and visibly supports information risk management.
effectiveness_notes: While we do engage in forward planning, the limited budgets available mean that we don't and likely never will have sufficient resources available.; The ISMS and SWG are very effective at this with CIRKS providing the management information to drive the process; The ISMS is operating correctly and is enforced by CIRKS reporting

title: Security objectives and measurement
description: Measurable security objectives are set, and performance against them is tracked and reported to senior leadership.
effectiveness_notes: We are fully defined at this point and the system will reach optimising once the first annual cycle is complete

title: Corrective action and improvement
description: Shortfalls found through audits, incidents or reviews are recorded, their causes are fixed, and the lessons are used to improve the organisation's approach.
effectiveness_notes: Partially delivered via CIRKS gap assessment reports. This needs to be augmented with additional 3rd party verification.; Currently this only exists as a written policy. It is new and has yet to operate the full process cycle to completion.

title: Risk strategy and appetite
description: Senior leadership sets the organisation's risk appetite and its preferred ways of responding to risk, considers opportunities as well as threats, makes information risk part of the organisation's wider risk management, and reviews the strategy regularly.
effectiveness_notes: The CIRKS management information reports provide detailed evidence to the corporate risk management process; Currently accumulating evidence in CIRKS, but we'll have to wait until the first annual review to measure how effective this is.

title: Information asset register
description: All information assets are recorded with their owner, location, impact level and the systems that process them.
effectiveness_notes: This is one of the positive side effects of the CIRKS system that has required the IAOs to rate all the critical assets; CIRKS is the definitive source for this information

title: Systems register
description: All systems, including cloud services, are recorded with their owner, purpose, hosting location and the information assets they process.
effectiveness_notes: ME365 is responsible for maintaining this on the majority of systems. Coverage is not 100% at the moment

title: Devices register
description: All devices that connect to the organisation's networks or information are recorded with their owner, type, location and configuration baseline.
effectiveness_notes: ME365 tracks a large proportion of the estate but we are not sure that this is sufficient

title: Software register
description: Software approved for use is recorded, ideally using automated inventory tools, and the organisation knows which versions are installed and where.

title: Registers are kept current
description: The registers are kept current, using automated discovery to find devices and software that are not recorded, and are reviewed periodically. Anything unrecorded or unauthorised is investigated and removed or approved.

title: Asset return and disposal
description: Assets are returned when people leave or change role, and equipment and storage media are disposed of securely so information cannot be recovered.

title: AI use policy
description: The organisation has a policy that sets out the acceptable use of AI, how users gain access to AI tools and their obligations when using them.

title: AI usage is documented
description: AI usage is recorded centrally so the organisation can say who is using AI, where it is installed and what information and systems it can access.

title: AI usage is approved
description: Use of AI to process an information asset is approved by that asset's owner before it begins.

title: AI agents operate with unique accounts
description: Each AI agent that operates autonomously runs under its own account, so its access can be authorised and its actions contained and audited separately from any person.

title: AI agent access is controlled
description: AI agents are confined to their operating environment and given only the access they need to do their job (least privilege).

title: AI monitoring
description: Environments where AI agents operate are covered by the organisation's detective monitoring, in line with the AI use policy.

title: AI outputs are reviewed
description: Outputs from AI that are used to make decisions, or are published, are reviewed by a person to a degree that matches their impact.

title: AI services are assessed
description: Third-party AI services are assessed under the third party information risk policy before use, including where information is sent and whether it is used to train the supplier's models.

title: Data classification policy
description: Information is classified using the department impact tables, marked where appropriate, and its classification is recorded in the information asset register.

title: Data handling policy
description: Rules set out how information at each impact level is protected when stored, processed and transmitted, including who may access it and how it may be shared.

title: Encryption policy, standards, procedures and guidelines
description: The organisation defines when encryption is required, which algorithms and key lengths are approved, and how keys are created, stored, changed and withdrawn.

title: Protection of data at rest
description: Stored information is protected in line with its impact level, including encryption of devices, removable media and backups where required.

title: Protection of data in transit
description: Information is protected when it moves across networks or between organisations, using approved encryption and transfer methods.
effectiveness_notes: TLS 1.3 is on everything. We have an internal CA with an HSM protected key. We have a policy in place and we audit systems against this requirement

title: Protection of data during processing
description: Information in use is protected by limiting who and what can access it, masking it where full values are not needed, and keeping live data out of test environments unless approved.

title: Data retention and deletion
description: Information is kept only for as long as it is needed and is securely deleted at the end of its retention period.

title: Personal data protection
description: Personal data is identified in the information asset register and handled in line with data protection law.

title: Data leakage prevention
description: Measures are in place to detect and prevent high-impact information leaving the organisation without authorisation.

title: Legal, regulatory and licensing obligations
description: The legal, regulatory and contractual requirements that apply to the organisation's information are identified and met, including software licences and intellectual property.
effectiveness_notes: this is reviewed annually by the legal team

title: Data flows are documented
description: The movement of high-impact information between systems, locations and organisations is documented, so that each flow can be protected and its risks assessed.

title: Personal devices use
description: Personal devices which are not under the full control of the organisation are not permitted to access or store the organisation's data. BYOD is a bad idea

title: Organisation access to personal data
description: Where an organisation has control over a personal device, they do not have the ability to access or delete the data which is the personal property of the device owner. BYOD is a bad idea

title: Device hardening policy and standard
description: Secure configuration baselines are defined for each type of device and system, removing unnecessary services, accounts and default settings. The goal being to reduce the attack surface of all devices.
effectiveness_notes: We have hardening standards which are applied and monitored by the Wazuh

title: Configuration monitoring
description: Devices and systems are checked against their baseline, and any departure from it is detected and either corrected or approved.

title: Configuration change control
description: Changes to configuration are assessed, approved and recorded before they are made.
effectiveness_notes: Our change control is good when the IT team are involved, but there is a lot of SHiT in operation for some departments which we cannot vouch for

title: Malware protection
description: Devices are protected against malicious software and exploits by centrally managed, behaviour-based protection that updates automatically, scans removable media and cannot be switched off by users.

title: Removable media and ports
description: The use of removable media and device ports is restricted to approved devices.

title: Mobile and portable devices
description: Laptops, phones and tablets lock after repeated failed log-in attempts, can be wiped remotely if lost, and keep the organisation's information separate from personal use.

title: Device physical protection
description: Device consoles are set to lock after a defined period of time set by the device hardening standard. Devices that are a risk of physical theft encrypt their data. Physical protection is provided for publicly accessible equipment

title: Automated vulnerability scanning
description: The organisation establishes one or more network based vulnerability scanning tools which can identify system configuration anomalies and vulnerable network services

title: Vulnerability management policy and process
description: The organisation defines how software vulnerabilities are identified, prioritised and fixed, with target timescales for each level of severity. Software vulnerabilities are analysed on a periodic basis and prioritised based on risk values.

title: Vulnerabilities are identified
description: Internal and internet-facing systems are scanned regularly using automated tools, and vendor and security advisories are monitored for all software in the software register.

title: Patching within target timescales
description: Security updates for operating systems, applications and network equipment are applied within the timescales set in the vulnerability management policy, using automated patching where possible.

title: Unsupported software and hardware
description: Software and hardware no longer supported by the vendor is removed or replaced, or the risk of keeping it is recorded as an exception.
effectiveness_notes: Depends on the annual budget and how many spare systems we have

title: Exceptions are risk managed
description: Where a vulnerability cannot be fixed in time, the risk is recorded in the risk register along with any compensating controls.

title: Software installation is controlled
description: Only approved software, libraries, scripts and browser or email extensions can be installed or run, and only people authorised to do so can install them.
effectiveness_notes: Fully controlled on all platforms by Crowdstrike agent

title: Identity management policy
description: The organisation has a policy for how identities are created, managed and removed for people, services and AI agents, using central account management where possible.
effectiveness_notes: Everything is MFA via AD or Azure. There may be some outliers

title: Unique identities
description: Every person and service has a unique identity and all accounts are recorded. Shared accounts are not used, or where unavoidable they are approved and their use can be traced to an individual.

title: Joiners, movers and leavers
description: Identities are verified before credentials are issued, and identities and their access are set up, changed and removed promptly as people join, change role and leave.
effectiveness_notes: All on-boarding follows the HR processes which always include proper identification of employees.

title: Strong authentication
description: The strength of authentication matches the risk, with multi-factor authentication for internet-facing applications, remote access, privileged accounts and high-impact information.

title: Authentication information is protected
description: Passwords, other secrets and the tokens used for single sign-on are unique, issued, stored and changed securely, protected in use and never shared.
effectiveness_notes: This is fully implemented

title: Service and system accounts
description: Non-human accounts each have a named owner and documented purpose, and their credentials are held securely.

title: Central log of accounts
description: The organisation maintains a central log of accounts. The log identifies where accounts are managed, including central authentication services (e.g. Active Directory), cloud authentication and local machine identification. The log identifies every account granted to a named user in under 5 minutes, so that accounts can be deactivated rapidly.

title: Access control policy
description: The organisation has a policy that sets out how access to information and systems is requested, approved, granted and removed, based on defined roles and managed centrally where possible.

title: Access is authorised
description: Access is granted only with the approval of a manager or system owner, based on a business need. Granting of access is documented and traceable.

title: Least privilege
description: People and services are given only the access they need to do their job.
effectiveness_notes: We have an operational AS which is well established and in use on many systems. We have processes for the identification of users

title: Privileged access is managed
description: Administrative and other privileged access is restricted, held in separate accounts, approved and closely monitored.

title: Access is reviewed
description: Managers and system owners review access regularly, disable dormant accounts and remove anything no longer needed.

title: Segregation of duties
description: Conflicting duties are split between different people so no one person can misuse a system or process undetected.

title: Remote access
description: Remote access is approved, made only from managed or approved devices through the organisation's secure remote access service, and protected by strong authentication.

title: Privileged utility programs
description: Tools that can override system or application controls are restricted to authorised administrators and their use is logged.

title: Traceable user identities
description: All accounts granted to a user are centrally identifiable using a consistent user identity.

title: Role based access control (RBAC)
description: Access to resources is based on the role a user has within the organisation. The use of RBAC simplifies the management of access

title: Monitoring policy
description: The organisation defines what is monitored, why, by whom and how alerts are handled. A logging standard is developed for systems which defines the minimum set of

title: Logging policy
description: Security-relevant events are logged across systems, devices, applications and networks, including access to high-impact information, DNS and web requests and administrative commands.

title: Log aggregation and storage
description: Logs are aggregated and collected centrally, protected from tampering, given enough storage and kept for a defined period.
effectiveness_notes: We have centralised logging services and plenty of capacity available.

title: Application specific logging
description: Logging is defined for each application based on what the application does. Sensitive actions likely to be targeted by attackers are identified and logged.

title: Clock synchronisation
description: System clocks are synchronised to an agreed time source so events can be correlated between systems.

title: Monitoring coverage
description: Monitoring coverage, including logs from cloud and other service providers, is checked against the systems register and devices register, and any gaps are recorded as risks.
effectiveness_notes: We have basic monitoring in place on the VPN termination and some log analysis to watch for strange behaviours.

title: Detection of malware and viruses
description: Devices are monitored using host based agents which can detect the presence and activity of malicious code and viruses

title: Detection and prevention of malicious activity
description: Devices are monitored using host based agents which can detect suspicious activity by users and agents and take preventative action to limit damage.
effectiveness_notes: We have excellent tools in place but we are somewhat limited in terms of our ability to operate extended SOC hours; Provided by the Crowdstrike EPP solutions

title: Central monitoring team
description: All detective monitoring events are fed to a common function. The staff managing this a trained to identity suspicious events and take actions to limit damage. The staff have detective monitoring responsibilities documented in their job responsibilities and sufficient time each day to meet these primary objectives.
effectiveness_notes: CTI is included in many of the products and the supplier feeds, It is not done in the context of who is specifically targeting us as an organisation.; We feed everything to a common set of tools, but these remain unintegrated.; We're a small team so this is enabled by co-location of teams; Wazuh is developing but we have layers of additional integration remaining before we can hit the highest maturity

title: Backup policy
description: The organisation defines what is backed up, how often and how long backups are kept, based on the impact of the information. Backups run automatically.

title: Backups are protected
description: Backups are encrypted and stored separately from live systems, with at least one copy offline or unchangeable so it survives a ransomware attack.
effectiveness_notes: Veem is deployed everywhere and it  is regularly tested and used for restoration of services

title: Restores are tested
description: Restoring from backup is tested regularly to prove that information and systems can be recovered within the required time, and backups are checked for integrity before they are used. Backups are tested to demonstrate successful cold start restoration of critical services

title: Recovery objectives
description: System owners set how quickly each system is to be restored and how much data loss is acceptable, based on its impact.

title: Redundancy
description: Critical systems are replicated or duplicated so that a single failure does not stop the service.
effectiveness_notes: This is well managed for Department of Communications systems. We know ShIT systems exist but these are not assessed

title: Continuity and recovery plans
description: Plans set out how critical services are kept running or recovered during disruption, and the plans are exercised.

title: Capacity management
description: The capacity of systems, storage and networks is monitored and planned so that services are not disrupted by running out of resources.
effectiveness_notes: IT Director core activity is capacity planning

title: Security awareness programme
description: Everyone receives security awareness training when they join and at regular intervals afterwards, covering at least passwords and authentication, handling information, avoiding accidental exposure, spotting missing security updates, the dangers of insecure networks and reporting incidents.
effectiveness_notes: We have good regular training but there are some senior managers who seem to forget that they should be setting an example

title: Role-based training
description: People in specialist roles, such as administrators, developers, information asset owners and risk analysts, are trained for their security responsibilities.
effectiveness_notes: Moderate

title: Phishing and social engineering
description: Staff are taught to recognise and report phishing and other social engineering, and their awareness is tested.

title: Training is tracked
description: Completion of training is recorded and followed up, and the results are used to improve the programme.

title: Pre-employment screening
description: Background checks are carried out on staff and contractors before they start, to a depth that matches the impact of the information they will access.

title: Security responsibilities are agreed
description: Staff and contractors agree to their security responsibilities, including confidentiality, as part of their terms of engagement.
effectiveness_notes: HR mandates the completion of InfoSec training for all staff and contractors

title: Disciplinary process
description: A formal disciplinary process exists for breaches of security policy, and staff know about it.

title: Leavers and role changes
description: When people leave or change role, their access is removed or changed, assets are returned and they are reminded of security duties that continue, such as confidentiality.

title: Third party information risk policy
description: The organisation has a policy that sets out how information risk from suppliers is assessed and managed throughout the relationship, and supplier risks are recorded in the risk register alongside other risks.
effectiveness_notes: Policies in place, program not defined or funded. however this will improve as the new policy; We have a policy and the procurement process include InfoSec as a stakeholder. This will gradually improve

title: Suppliers are recorded
description: Suppliers with access to the organisation's information or systems are recorded, along with what they can access and its impact level.

title: Suppliers are assessed
description: Suppliers are assessed before they are engaged, to a depth that matches the impact of what they will access.
effectiveness_notes: This now happens for new suppliers but it will likely take years before all existing contracts have been subject to review; This now functions for all new suppliers but it derated because we have some many legacy suppliers who have not yet been subject to the new conditions.

title: Security requirements in contracts
description: Contracts set out the supplier's security obligations, including incident notification and the right to audit.
effectiveness_notes: Actually well established for new suppliers but we have many existing suppliers who are not yet ready for review.

title: Suppliers are audited
description: Supplier security is reviewed during the relationship, and significant changes to the service are assessed.

title: Cloud services
description: Cloud services are assessed and configured to the organisation's requirements, and responsibilities are clearly divided between the organisation and the provider.

title: Supplier access is contained
description: Suppliers' access to systems, information assets and premises is limited by technical controls that enforce the principle of least privilege

title: Supplier exit
description: When a contract ends, supplier access is removed and the organisation's information is returned or securely destroyed.
effectiveness_notes: In place in our new contracts but not in our existing supply agreements

title: Trusted products
description: Hardware and software are bought from trusted sources and checked for authenticity and integrity before they are used.

title: Supplier activity is monitored
description: System and networks log access and activity from supplier accounts. Supplier account activity can be quickly associated with each supplier inside detective monitoring systems.

title: Secure development policy
description: The organisation defines the security practices that apply at each stage of software development.

title: Security requirements
description: Security requirements are identified, using threat modelling where appropriate, and agreed before software is designed or bought.

title: Secure design and coding
description: Software is designed and written to agreed secure principles and coding standards, using proven, vetted components for security functions such as authentication and encryption.

title: Security testing
description: Software is security tested before release, including automated code checks and security testing where the impact justifies it, and the issues found are fixed or risk accepted.

title: Separate environments
description: Development, test and live environments are kept separate, and access to live is restricted.

title: Source code is protected
description: Access to source code is controlled, and changes are tracked and reviewed.

title: Third-party components
description: Libraries and other components used in software come from trusted sources, are kept up to date and recorded, and are checked for known vulnerabilities.

title: Change and release control
description: Changes to live software are approved, tested and recorded, and can be rolled back.

title: Outsourced development
description: Software developed by suppliers meets the same security requirements as in-house work.

title: Vulnerability reports are handled
description: There is a clear way for anyone to report vulnerabilities in the organisation's software. Reports are rated for severity, fixed, and their root causes addressed so they do not recur.
effectiveness_notes: We have the tools established but we're still lacking skilled staff to achieve full maturity

title: Incident response plan
description: A plan sets out roles, responsibilities and steps for handling security incidents, including which suppliers are involved, contact details, and how the team will communicate if normal systems are unavailable.
effectiveness_notes: We have written down our incident response playbooks and tested some of them against workshop scenarios. We are yet to undertake a full scale test.

title: Incident reporting
description: Everyone knows how to report a suspected incident and is encouraged to do so quickly.

title: Assessment and triage
description: Reported events are assessed promptly against defined criteria to decide whether they are incidents, how serious they are and whether they need to be escalated.
effectiveness_notes: We have a well established and tested process for natural disasters that we follow . We have adapted this process to manage cyber incidents; Everything is submitted via the ticketing system where a set of standard procedures are predetermined to follow on activity; This is defined in the incident response policy and triggered in the playbooks.; This is defined in the policies and the playbooks.; This is a repeat of the other incident playbook driven processes; IN as much as CIRKS provides a rating for all the systems within

title: Containment and recovery
description: Incidents are contained, their cause removed and affected services restored in line with the plan.
effectiveness_notes: The network isolation is fully implemented but the detection and action on processes are not tested properly of fully robust.

title: Evidence is preserved
description: Evidence and investigation actions are recorded and kept in a way that preserves their integrity, in case they are needed for disciplinary or legal action.
effectiveness_notes: This is repeatable and recorded in the documentation and emails exchanged so we can say it is possible but not fully robust.; This is aspirational at this point. In the event of the next incident the playbooks identify this as a requirement but we haven't tested this in anger yet.

title: External notification
description: Obligations to notify regulators, authorities and affected people are known and met within required timescales.
effectiveness_notes: Not really done in any meaningful way; This is standard part of our organisation

title: Lessons learned
description: Each significant incident is reviewed to establish what happened and its root cause, and the lessons are fed into the risk register and security action plan.
effectiveness_notes: We do this on a best endeavours basis but we are a small organisation and have limited ability to do this

title: Plans are exercised
description: The incident response plan is exercised and updated with what is learned.

title: Recovery is managed
description: Recovery from an incident starts and ends against defined criteria. Restored systems are checked before they return to normal use, progress is reported to the people who need to know, and public statements use approved messages.
effectiveness_notes: This is covered by the play books but we still don't have a full end to end test completed; Everything is in placed but full testing and lessons learned still haven't been complete; Covered by the playbooks but untested at this time

title: Information risk assessments
description: Risk assessments are carried out for new systems and significant changes, using the risk rating methodology, and are reviewed periodically.
effectiveness_notes: this is a core feature of CIRKS

title: Security testing programme
description: Internal and external risk assessments and other technical security assessments (penetration tests) are planned and carried out regularly, based on risk, to confirm that security measures are in place and operating as expected.

title: Findings are tracked
description: Findings from assessments and tests are recorded in the risk register or security action plan and followed through to closure.
effectiveness_notes: We have regular security testing and continuous vulnerability detection in place.

title: Testing is controlled
description: Security testing is scoped, authorised and carried out so that it does not damage live systems or expose information.

title: Independent review
description: The organisation's approach to information security is reviewed independently at planned intervals.

title: Compliance checks
description: Compliance with security policies and standards is checked regularly, and any shortfalls are addressed.

title: Network security policy
description: The organisation has a documented architecture that sets out how its networks are designed, protected and managed, and keeper up-to-date.

title: Network policy enforcement (firewalls)
description: Traffic between networks, and to and from servers and end-user devices, is allowed only where there is an approved business need. Network traffic policy (firewall rules) is documented and explained, and rule sets are simple enough to remove ambiguity.
effectiveness_notes: Our zero trust network pattern is primarily responsible for this control

title: Device identification and network access (802.1X)
description: Device identity is established when devices connect to sensitive systems or networks.

title: Zoning and segregation
description: Networks are divided into zones based on impact and function, so that a compromise in one zone is contained.

title: Network services are secured
description: Network services are designed to counter the threats they face. Controls are selected and operated based on documented security architecture decisions.

title: Wireless networks
description: Wireless networks are secured to prevent exposure of traffic to eavesdropping. Basic password access to a wireless SSID does not establish device trust.

title: Web and email filtering
description: Access to harmful websites is blocked using trusted, filtered DNS and web filtering. Email is filtered for malicious content, unnecessary file types and spoofing.

title: Network traffic volumetric
description: Volumetric data is generated for all network traffic to detect significant flows of data that are out of the ordinary and may indicate unapproved data exfiltration.

title: Network Intrusion Detection and Prevention
description: Network activity is monitored to identify suspicious activity, provide alerts and possibly trigger preventative responses. The capability is centrally monitored by the detective monitoring team
effectiveness_notes: We have extensive coverage at the network layer

title: Secure administration
description: Systems and network equipment are managed using secure, encrypted protocols, from dedicated devices used only for administration.

title: Administrative accounts should have no email access and minimal access to the Internet
description: Systems administration accounts do not have access to email and only very limited access to the Internet.

title: Establish global trust in encrypted external services
description: Communications outside the organisation are protected from spoofing using recognised technical controls. Encrypted services use PKI-based trust from a recognised public trust authority.

title: Establish global trust in DNS domains
description: The organisation's DNS is protected from illegal modification and impersonation using DNSSEC.

title: Establish global trust in email
description: Email authenticity is protected using SPF to identify legitimate sending servers (preventing address spoofing) and DKIM to prove message authenticity.

title: Physical security perimeters
description: Buildings and areas holding information or equipment have defined perimeters with protection that matches the impact of the information assets and systems they contain.

title: Physical entry is controlled
description: Entry to the organisation's premises and secure areas is limited to authorised people, and visitors are escorted. All user access is recorded in timed entry logs (ideally electronically)
effectiveness_notes: This was hard to assess because we have multiple locations which have physical key access but no record of the key holders.

title: Secure areas
description: Rules for working in secure areas are defined based upon identified threats.Users in these spaces understand these rules and workspaces are regularly audited for compliance.

title: Physical security monitoring
description: Premises are monitored, for example by alarms or CCTV, so that unauthorised entry is detected.

title: Environmental threats
description: Premises and equipment are protected against fire, flood, extreme temperature and other environmental threats.

title: Equipment siting and supporting utilities
description: Equipment is sited and protected to reduce risk, and is supported by reliable power, cooling and other utilities.

title: Cabling security
description: Power and network cables are protected from interception, interference and damage.

title: Equipment maintenance
description: Equipment is maintained correctly, and information is protected when equipment is serviced or sent away for repair.

title: Clear desk and clear screen
description: Papers and removable media are put away and screens are locked when unattended.

title: Assets off-premises
description: Devices and information taken off-site are protected against loss, theft and overlooking.
